sources.entry: socks5-proxy-server - SOCKS5 proxy server with built-in authentication and Telegram-bot for user management and user statistics on data spent (handy when you pay per GB of data). It is dockerised and simple to install. Apache-2.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: A dockerised SOCKS5 proxy server with username/password authentication, per-user data usage statistics, and a Telegram bot for managing users.
summary.what_it_does:
Runs a SOCKS5 proxy server on a configurable port (default 54321) that can require authentication so anonymous users are refused. Users are created, deleted, and listed through CLI scripts executed inside the Docker container (create-user.js, delete-user.js, users-stats.js). A Telegram bot provides the same administration from chat, including commands for user statistics, creating and deleting users, listing users, and generating random passwords. Admins are created and removed with separate scripts. The bot can use either webhooks (which require SSL certificates, per the README) or polling. Configuration is via a .env file copied from .env.example.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="how_to_run">["Install Docker", "cp .env.example .env", "Edit .env (APP_PORT, LOG_LEVEL, REQUIRE_AUTH; and PUBLIC_URL, TELEGRAM_API_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL, TELEGRAM_USE_WEBHOOKS for the bot)", "docker compose up -d", "docker exec -it <proxy-container> sh -c 'exec node scripts/create-user.js'", "docker exec -it <telegram-bot-container> sh -c 'exec node scripts/create-admin.js'"]
use_cases: Run a SOCKS5 proxy with login credentials on a personal server
Share a proxy with a small group of users and control who can connect
Track how much data each proxy user has consumed
Administer proxy users from a Telegram chat instead of the command line
Run a cheap proxy where the operator pays per GB of traffic and needs per-user accounting
notable: Built-in username/password authentication with an option to disallow anonymous access
Per-user data usage statistics, useful when paying per GB
Telegram bot for user management, statistics, and random password generation
Admin accounts can be created and removed via scripts
Docker-based setup with a .env configuration file
caveats: Webhook mode needs SSL certificates; polling is the alternative
Setup requires a BotFather token and a public URL for the Telegram bot features
Administration is by docker exec scripts or the Telegram bot; no web UI is mentioned in the README
License is taken from the awesome-selfhosted listing metadata, not confirmed in the README text
